title: SRE reliability huddle prep - quick notes
content:
Quick brain dump / meeting prep for Friday SRE ops sync (30m) - notes to self and agenda.

Context: last week saw a bump in pages and two Sev2s related to cache behavior and routing fallbacks. Need to focus on immediate mitigations, SLO health, and oncall fatigue indicators. Keep this tight — > cover incidents, SLO state, paging trends, action items, and 2 blockers for next week.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: Quick wins & shoutouts (reduce noise, ownership wins)
- 8m: SLO snapshot + anomalies (what tripped, where; call out SLOs drifting)
- 8m: Top incidents recap (new learnings, current status of RCA/mitigation)
- 6m: Paging trend analysis + runbook gaps (where ops load is growing)
- 3m: Assign actions + next steps.

SLO snapshot (current at 2026-03-26 08:00 UTC):
- inference-api (hosted): availability target 99.95% (rolling 30d) -> current 99.88% (delta -0.07). P95 latency target <120ms -> current p95 = 140ms. P99 = 640ms (not great). Primary driver: queuing during burst windows and a couple of model cold-start OOM retries.
- dedicated-gpu-pool (throughput): target: 99.9% of requests served under throughput SLO -> current 99.92 (ok). However some tenants saw request requeues leading to increased tail latency.
- control-plane write ops: target 99.99 -> current 99.995 (fine).

Paging trends (7d window):
- Total pages: 132 (↑18% wk/wk). Increase concentrated on late-night PST window (02:00-05:00 UTC).
- Noise sources: frequent alerts from cache-hit-ratio threshold (many transient dips), and model-serving OOM suspect.
- Oncall load: median pages per engineer = 3/day, but top quartile saw 7/day (Arjun flagged burnout risk).

Top incidents (brief summaries):
1) inc-2026-03-18-cache-thrashing (Sev2)
   - Symptom: dramatic drop in prefix/KV cache hit ratio with cascading extra compute, higher GC on hosts, elevated request latency and retries.
   - Root cause (initial): regressed cache eviction policy after a runtime change (PR #2142) that changed LRU heuristics for multi-tenant workloads.
   - Mitigation applied: rolled back the PR on 2026-03-18 03:30 UTC; manual warmup for hot prefixes; temporary raise of cache-size soft limit.
   - Next: formal RCA (Arjun) due EOD 2026-03-29, follow-up CI test to cover eviction scenarios.

2) inc-2026-03-22-routing-fallback-loop (Sev2)
   - Symptom: under sustained high utilization, the policy engine incorrectly promoted a fallback variant that in turn triggered more fallbacks (loop), causing request duplication and pagination to SLO.
   - Mitigation: tuned promotion thresholds; patched policy to add hysteresis; throttling for fallback triggers introduced.
   - Next: add a unit/integration test to simulate fallback churn (Liam), and add metrics to detect early signs (new metric: fallback-rate/s).

3) inc-2026-03-24-model-oom-burst (Sev3 -> near Sev2)
   - Symptom: a recent model variant (v2.7-q4) OOMed in cold-starts when batch sizes aggregated unexpectedly (rare path in batcher).
   - Mitigation: temporary rollback to v2.6 for affected tenants; enforced conservative batch caps for cold-starts.
   - Next: change batcher estimation logic (Priya) and add a small-scale chaos test for cold-starts. Target PR and deploy by 2026-04-02.

Runbook & observability gaps identified:
- Cache eviction runbook is thin: no clear 'if hit-ratio dips then...' escalation path. Need a one-pager for oncall. (Owner: Maya)
- No dedicated alert for 'fallback promotion oscillation' — currently we see latency but not the promotion churn signal. Add fallback-rate alert (Owner: Liam).
- Cold-start OOMs only surface as host-level OOMs; need model-level instrumentation (heap/kv usage, batch shape stats) to detect pre-failure. (Owner: Priya)

Questions to bring up in sync:
- Should we lower the cache eviction aggressiveness globally while we finish the eviction fix? Tradeoff: memory pressure vs latency.
- For fallback hysteresis change, do we need a temporary dashboard for customers on Dedicated to explain degraded tail latency?
- Are our paging thresholds configured to group similar noisy pages (i.e., combine transient cache dips) to reduce noise?

Quick metrics to show (prepare graphs before the meeting):
- 30d rolling availability vs SLO (inference-api) with annotations for the three incidents.
- Pages per engineer (7d) histogram.
- Cache hit ratio heatmap by tenant for last 14d.
- Fallback promotion rate over last 7d, with policy changes annotated.

Action items (assignments, due dates):
- Arjun: full RCA for cache-thrashing (inc-2026-03-18). Deliverable: one-pager + test plan. Due 2026-03-29.
- Liam: implement fallback-rate metric + alert, and add integration test for promotion oscillation. Due 2026-04-01.
- Priya: batcher cold-start cap fix + chaos test plan. PR by 2026-03-30, deploy by 2026-04-02.
- Maya (me): draft cache eviction runbook (oncall playbook snippet), and push to Confluence. Due 2026-03-31.
- Ops: temporarily set cache eviction soft limit + monitor impact (ops-change-id: OPS-789). Verify memory pressure by 2026-03-27. (Assign Ops rotation)

Notes to self / talking points:
- Emphasize that core availability is still within close bounds but tail latency is where users feel it; quantify user impact with example tenant metrics.
- Keep customer-facing messaging minimal: "we identified intermittent cache eviction behavior and reduced tail latency with rollback; working on permanent fix". No blame.
- Ask platform/product: do we want customer-visible rollout notes for the model rollback? Who drafts? (ping Zoe from product-hosted-api)

Meeting outputs expected:
- Confirm owners & dates for each action item.
- Agree on a short list of alerts to silence/adjust this week to reduce noise.
- Decide whether to reduce eviction aggressiveness (ops decision) and communicate to oncall.

Backlog items (longer term):
- Model-level memory telemetry (Priya)
- Eviction policy rework with synthetic workloads (Arjun + infra)
- Batcher rewrite for more conservative cold-start behavior (Q2 planning)

End notes / random reminders:
- Pull the "pages per engineer" raw data from PagerDuty exports; prepare a simple CSV to show distribution.
- Check if any Dedicated customers filed support tickets correlated to the Sev2s — if so, coordinate CS outreach.

Unresolved questions for follow-up:
- If we globally relax eviction aggressiveness, what is the expected increase in host memory usage? Need infra calc. (ask infra team for mem headroom numbers)
- Are there tenants who still run on v2.7-q4 who were missed by the rollback? Quick scan required.

Okay that's it — keep it as a sketch for the Friday huddle. Will tidy before posting to Confluence.

Maya
